walls.notes: St Andrew the Great, south (St Tibbs Row) side: buff ashlar Gothic Revival (1842-3) with stepped buttresses (as pilasters) dividing four bays, each with a tall pointed three-light traceried window with leaded glazing; plinth with offset at ~1.2 m and a plain parapet. Seen raking from the east end only; bay positions spaced evenly over the wall.

St Andrew the Great, east end on St Andrew's Street (p0 = south corner): buff ashlar gable with a corner buttress (pilaster) at the south corner and one large pointed Perpendicular east window (about four/five lights, sill ~3.6 m) centred in the wall; plinth offset ~1.2 m. walls.json eave (6.3 m) is below the window head; the real gable is ~10 m+ (eave fix should lift it). From Geograph 4363662.
